narrative: Material PL3__M1B41D26 exhibits high demand variability (CV=0.65) with a 76.75% non-zero fraction and unstable lead times (CV=0.70, range 0.14–5.18 days). The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock and orders at MOQ only, generating ~90 orders/year and leaving the material exposed to stockout risk. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with SS=815 and OQ=3,696 (storage-capped from EOQ=6,454) reduces annual cost by 58.6% while formally guaranteeing 95% service level. Storage capacity is the binding constraint and should be reviewed to unlock further EOQ savings.
warnings: Storage constraint is binding: EOQ 6454 capped to 3696 units (max_storage_units=4511.903, safety_stock=815)
Storage utilization at ~100% after each replenishment — no buffer for demand surges
SAP safety stock is zero — no stockout protection in current ERP configuration
Lead time CV=0.70 (unstable) — occasional spikes to 5+ days drive safety stock requirement

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous (non-zero 77% of working days) with high but not intermittent variability; (r,Q) is optimal for this profile as it triggers replenishment at a fixed reorder point r=1378 with a fixed quantity Q=3696, consolidating the excess ordering frequency of the current MOQ-only approach.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds hard: safety_stock + order_quantity = 4511 ≈ max_storage_units. Any upward safety-stock revision (e.g. using robust SS=1044) would require reducing order quantity below 3468, further limiting consolidation benefits. Recommend a storage capacity review.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (1068) + safety_stock (815) = 1883 < max_storage_units (4511.9), so the MOQ-capacity constraint is feasible. No infeasibility escalation required.
